item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption explains corruption risks in agencies’ internal supplier panels.
item.support: explains the key corruption risks associated with forming, using and maintaining supplier panels.

item.text: It examines how suppliers are selected, how work is allocated and how panels are maintained.
item.support: supplier-panel procurement can be divided into three phases

item.text: The Commission cautions that weaknesses in selecting panel members can leave later purchasing vulnerable to corruption.
item.support: if the processes used to establish the panel in Phase 1 are flawed

item.text: The Commission recommends formal contracting arrangements and a panel administrator to monitor purchasing, prices, due diligence and conflicts of interest.
item.support: the Commission recommends that an agency’s legal or contract management staff be involved in executing the necessary contractual arrangements.

item.quote: Agencies should therefore treat formation of a supplier panel with the same level of formality and probity as a procurement exercise.
